None of this changes the qualitative verdict (leverage reads 'Adequate'/'within normal range' under every basis), but it is a real, uncorrected inconsistency in a rating-driving anchor (feeds the §24 Filter-3 survival test cited in the Headline Scorecard) and should be reconciled to a single canonical figure before the next refresh.

notes: ciq_facts.json (the deterministic CIQ cross-check sidecar) could not be generated in this environment: the system Python is 3.9.6, and .claude/tools/ciq.py requires enum.StrEnum (Python 3.11+). This is an environment limitation, not a pool defect — noted per the command's own best-effort fallback ('ciq_facts unavailable'). All Section A/B/C checks in this report were instead performed via the deterministic resolve_citations.py tool against the full pool-extract corpus (/tmp/corpus.txt, rebuilt fresh via extract_pool.py — 21 sources, 7 workbooks, 51 tabs, 65 extracts, 0 extraction failures) plus direct reads of the cited primary-filing text. Aside from the net-debt/total-debt anchor conflict documented above, the run is unusually clean: every scenario-math check (CLAUDE.md §10) reconciles exactly, the base fair-value weighted blend and all three scenario EV-to-per-share bridges recompute correctly, the two most consequential governance-red-flag dollar figures (the $1,123M/$564M legal-reserve add-backs and the $6.4bn/$5.0bn DTA valuation-allowance releases) are both literal in the FY2025 10-K text (not merely vendor-sourced), the Delivery Hero deal terms are corroborated by both the 10-Q and an independent CIQ Key Developments entry, and the ROIC/WACC moat test is fully traceable to the CIQ Ratios tab with WACC correctly labeled as CAPM inference rather than miscited to a filing. No fabricated or wholly unsupported rating-driving figure was found, and no scenario or EV-bridge math was broken — the run does not qualify as 'Failed'. The net-debt anchor conflict is real, evidenced, and left unreconciled in the committed document, which is enough to withhold 'Clean'/'Minor issues' and warrants treating the balance-sheet leverage read as provisional until the ~$1.7bn total-debt gap (operating-lease treatment) and the short-term-investments netting mislabel are reconciled to one canonical figure.
